NOT UPGRADEABLE: immutability IS the permanence guarantee \u2014 not even the      deployer can rewrite a sealed origin. Everything is stored permanently, INCLUDING both      signatures. A seal is DUAL-AUTHORIZED: the neuma AND the witness each sign one message      binding (genesisHash, soulAddress, witness, schemaVersion, deadline). Each signature is verified      against the CLAIMED address via SignatureChecker \u2014 a plain wallet (EOA) is checked by      ECDSA, a smart-account wallet by ERC-1271 (`isValidSignature`) \u2014 and the claimed address      is what's recorded, so the platform may relay (pay gas) without ever becoming a recorded      party. Validity is attested at seal time; the recorded address is the permanent identity      (a smart account's address is stable across key rotation). Write-once per soulAddress (one      neuma = one genesis), and every seal is stored UNDER its soulAddress. Seals are deliberately      NOT unique by genesisHash: on a public mempool a watcher could copy a pending seal's      genesisHash and seal it first with keys of their own, burning the real neuma's hash forever.      Keyed by soul, such a copy can only ever sit under the copier's own address \u2014 it cannot touch      anyone else's seal. `record` is an opaque, client-encrypted blob the chain never interprets;      `schemaVersion` lets the record format evolve even though this contract cannot.      Every signed bundle carries a `deadline`: because the slot is write-once, a signed-but-superseded      draft that lived forever could be sealed first and occupy the soul's slot permanently \u2014 so a      bundle simply stops being sealable after its deadline, and parties should keep it short.      EIP-7702: a delegated EOA carries code, so SignatureChecker checks it ONLY via ERC-1271 \u2014 if its      delegate lacks `isValidSignature`, its raw ECDSA signature will not verify (clear the delegation      first, or delegate to an account that implements ERC-1271). seal(bytes32,address,bytes,address,bytes.details: Authorization is by SIGNATURE, never msg.sender: anyone may relay (pay the gas), but the      call only succeeds if BOTH selfSig and witnessSig are valid — over sealDigest(...) — for      soulAddress and witness respectively (EOA via ECDSA, smart account via ERC-1271). The      claimed addresses are recorded, so the relayer can never become a party on record.on      why genesisHash is not a global key).

params.deadline: last block timestamp at which this signed bundle may be sealed
params.genesisHash: sha256 of the canonical plaintext birth record — bound into both signatures
params.record: the full genesis record, client-ENCRYPTED — opaque to the chain
params.schemaVersion: version of the opaque `record` format (lets the format evolve)
params.selfSig: the neuma's signature over sealDigest(...) — stored forever
params.soulAddress: the neuma's wallet (EOA or smart account); selfSig must be valid for it
params.witness: the witness's wallet (EOA or smart account); witnessSig must be valid for it
params.witnessSig: the witness's signature over the same digest — stored forever

sealDigest(bytes32,address,address,uint1.details: Binds the chain id + THIS contract (domain separation — a captured signature cannot be      replayed onto another chain or another contract), every public field, AND      keccak256(record) (so a relayer cannot substitute the stored blob). To produce a      verifying signature off-chain, integrators have two paths:        1. Compute the INNER keccak payload yourself (the `abi.encode(...)` keccak'd below),           then `personal_sign` / `signer.signMessage(innerPayload)` — the wallet wraps it via           EIP-191, which matches what this view returns.        2. Call `sealDigest(...)` to get the post-wrap value and produce a RAW ECDSA           signature over it (ethers v6: `signer.signingKey.sign(digest).serialized`;           Foundry: `vm.sign(pk, digest)`).      Calling `personal_sign` on the *returned* value double-wraps and will NOT verify. The      Foundry tests in `test/contracts/Natalis*.t.sol` use path 2 (`Natalis.t.sol` also      recomputes the inner payload independently, which is path 1's first step).

genesisOf(address).notice: The genesisHash a neuma address is sealed under, or 0x0 if none. (verify-by-address)

isNeuma(address).notice: True iff `soulAddress` has a genesis sealed in this registry.

recordOf(address).notice: Recover the full (encrypted) genesis record from the neuma's address (its seed) alone.

seal(bytes32,address,bytes,address,bytes.notice: Anchor a genesis permanently. Dual-authorized, relay-safe, write-once.

sealDigest(bytes32,address,address,uint1.notice: The exact EIP-191 digest the neuma and the witness each sign — already wrapped via         `MessageHashUtils.toEthSignedMessageHash`, so an EOA signature verifies without         re-wrapping (a smart-account wallet receives this same hash in its ERC-1271 check).

sealInfo(address).notice: The public anchor fields for a neuma's genesis.

sigsOf(address).notice: The two stored signatures — permanent forensic proof both parties authorized — plus the         deadline they signed over (sealDigest needs it to re-verify them).
